    Parse latitude values

    Source: R/parse_lat.R
    parse_lat.Rd

    Parse latitude values

    Usage

    parse_lat(lat, format = NULL)

    Arguments

    lat

    (numeric/integer/character) one or more latitude values

    format

    (character) NULL (the default) or one or more patterns that say how the values are written, for example "DDMMSSH". With NULL, parzer finds the degrees, minutes and seconds by itself. Give a pattern when it cannot, for example when the digits are packed together with no separator, as in "512839N". With several patterns, each value is read with the first pattern that matches it. See the Format and Format examples sections.

    Value

    numeric vector

    Format

    A pattern describes how the values are written. It is made of letters and other characters. The idea comes from AngleFormat in Apache SIS and from CLongLatString.

    • D, M and S stand for the digits of the whole degrees, minutes and seconds. The number of letters is the exact number of digits: DD means exactly 2 digits, so it reads "05" but not "5", and DDD means exactly 3 digits, as longitudes often need. Values written without leading zeros need a second pattern, for example c("DD MM SSH", "D MM SSH") reads both "45 03 02N" and "5 03 02N". D is required. M and S are optional, but S needs M, and they come in the order D, M, S.

    • d, m and s stand for the decimal digits of the degrees, minutes or seconds. Only the last unit can have them. They come right after it, as in "DDMMmmm", or after a dot that follows it, as in "DDMM.m".

      • Without a dot, the decimal point is not written in the value. The number of letters is then the exact number of decimal digits: it is the only way to know where the hidden decimal point is. "HDDMMmmmmm" reads "N455698735" as N 45 degrees 56.98735 minutes.

      • After a dot, the value has a decimal point and one or more decimal digits, as many as you like: "DDMM.m" reads both "4556.9" and "4556.98735".

    • H stands for the hemisphere letter: N or S in parse_lat(), E or W in parse_lon(), in upper or lower case. S and W give a negative value. H can be at the start, at the end or in the middle, but only once. A letter of the other pair, for example E in parse_lat(), gives NA.

    • A space matches one or more spaces (or other white space).

    • Any other character, for example °, ', ", :, or a dot that is not followed by d, m or s, must be in the value exactly as in the pattern.

    • A sign can always be written right before the degrees: +, -, or a Unicode minus (U+2212), en dash – or em dash —. With H, the rules are the same as with format = NULL: "-45S" and "+45S" give -45, but "-45N" gives NA, because the minus sign and the letter disagree.

    Spaces at the start and at the end of a value are ignored. The pattern is matched against the value as it is given: the cleaning done with format = NULL, for example reading d or º as a degree mark, does not happen.

    A value gives NA when it does not match any pattern, when its minutes or seconds are 60 or more, or when the result is out of range (latitude outside -90/90, longitude outside -180/360). All these values are listed in one warning. They are not read again with format = NULL. A missing value (NA) or an empty string gives NA without a warning. A pattern that cannot work, for example "MMDD", "DDmmSS" or "DDX", is an error.

    Numbers are turned into text first, so they lose their leading zeros: parse_lon(0002741, format = "DDDMMSS") sees "2741" and gives NA. Give such values as text: parse_lon("0002741", format = "DDDMMSS").

    See the Format examples section for many examples.

    Format examples

    ValueformatResultWhy
    "512839N""DDMMSSH"51.4775ICAO latitude
    "4556.98735""DDMM.mmmmm"45.94979NMEA
    "4556.98735""DDMM.m"45.94979after a dot, any number of decimals
    "4556.9""DDMM.m"45.94833after a dot, any number of decimals
    "N455698735""HDDMMmmmmm"45.94979decimal point not written: exactly 5 decimals
    "2343 56N""DDMM SSH"23.73222
    "23 4356N""DD MMSSH"23.73222
    "23 4356N""DD MMSSH"23.73222a space matches several spaces
    "2343.5N""DDMM.mH"23.725
    "45N54.2356""DDHMM.m"45.90393H in the middle
    "s4530""HDDMM"-45.5H in front, in lower case
    "40°25'06\"N""DD°MM'SS\"H"40.41833symbols must match exactly
    "40:25:06""DD:MM:SS"40.41833
    "40.25""DD.MM"40.41667a dot before M is a plain dot
    "45.5""DD.d"45.5decimal degrees
    "-4530""DDMM"-45.5minus sign
    "\u22124530""DDMM"-45.5Unicode minus sign
    "-45S""DDH"-45sign and letter agree
    "+45S""DDH"-45the letter gives the sign
    "-45N""DDH"NAsign and letter disagree
    "45E""DDH"NAE is not a latitude letter
    "4530"c("DDMM", "DD MM")45.5the first pattern matches
    "45 30"c("DDMM", "DD MM")45.5the second pattern matches
    "453""DDMM"NA3 digits do not match 4 letters
    "45 03 02N"c("DD MM SSH", "D MM SSH")45.05056the first pattern matches
    "5 03 02N"c("DD MM SSH", "D MM SSH")5.05056no leading zero: the second pattern matches
    "5°3'2\"N""DD°MM'SS\"H"NADD needs exactly 2 digits
    "4575""DDMM"NA75 minutes
    "9000S""DDMMH"-90lowest latitude
    "9130""DDMM"NAlatitude above 90

    Errors

    Throws warnings on parsing errors, and returns NA in each case

    Types of errors:

    • invalid argument: e.g., letters passed instead of numbers, see https://en.cppreference.com/cpp/error/invalid_argument

    • out of range: numbers of out acceptable range, see https://en.cppreference.com/cpp/error/out_of_range

    • out of latitude range: not within -90/90 range

    • minutes or seconds out of range (negative or 60 and above): not within 0/60 range, e.g. "10 30,12345" is read as 10 degrees, 30 minutes and 12345 seconds, so it gives a warning and NA

    • a decimal degree or minute followed by another slot: only the last slot can be decimal, e.g. "45.5 30"

    • a minus sign that disagrees with the direction letter: minus sign and direction letter disagree, e.g. "N -45" or "-45N"

    • a number with two decimal points: invalid number, e.g. "40.25.30"

    • with format, a value that does not match any pattern: does not match format, see the Format section

    A comma or space is always a separator between degrees, minutes and seconds, never a decimal mark.

    Examples

    parse_lat("")
#> [1] NA

# with format: say how the values are written (see the Format section)
parse_lat("512839N", format = "DDMMSSH") # ICAO => 51.4775
#> [1] 51.4775
parse_lat("4556.98735", format = "DDMM.mmmmm") # NMEA => 45.94979
#> [1] 45.94979
# after a dot, any number of decimals
parse_lat(c("4556.9", "4556.98735"), format = "DDMM.m")
#> [1] 45.94833 45.94979
# no dot: 5 letters, so exactly 5 decimals => 45.94979
parse_lat("N455698735", format = "HDDMMmmmmm")
#> [1] 45.94979
parse_lat("2343 56N", format = "DDMM SSH") # => 23.73222
#> [1] 23.73222
parse_lat("23 4356N", format = "DD MMSSH") # => 23.73222
#> [1] 23.73222
parse_lat("2343.5N", format = "DDMM.mH") # => 23.725
#> [1] 23.725
parse_lat("45N54.2356", format = "DDHMM.m") # => 45.90393
#> [1] 45.90393
parse_lat("40°25'06\"N", format = "DD°MM'SS\"H") # => 40.41833
#> [1] 40.41833
parse_lat(c("-45S", "+45S"), format = "DDH") # => -45 -45
#> [1] -45 -45
parse_lat(4530, format = "DDMM") # numbers work too => 45.5
#> [1] 45.5
# several formats, tried in order for each value
parse_lat(c("4530", "45 30", "N4530"), format = c("DDMM", "DD MM", "HDDMM"))
#> [1] 45.5 45.5 45.5
# no leading zero: a second format with one D
parse_lat(c("45 03 02N", "5 03 02N"), format = c("DD MM SSH", "D MM SSH"))
#> [1] 45.050556  5.050556
# NA and one warning: sign and letter disagree, wrong letter, 75 minutes
parse_lat(c("-45N", "45E", "4575"), format = c("DDH", "DDMM"))
#> Warning: NA for 3 value(s) that could not be read with `format`:
#>   "-45N": minus sign and direction letter disagree
#>   "45E": direction letter must be N or S
#>   "4575": minutes or seconds not within 0/60 range
#> [1] NA NA NA
# without format, packed digits give NA and a warning that points to format
parse_lat("2343 56N")
#> Warning: not within -90/90 range, got: 2343 56n
#>   degrees, minutes and seconds may be packed together (e.g. DDMMSS): try the format argument of parse_lat() or parse_lon()
#> [1] NA

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
parse_lat("-91")
parse_lat("95")
parse_lat("asdfaf")

parse_lat("45")
parse_lat("-45")
parse_lat("-45.2323")

# out of range with std::stod?
parse_lat("-45.23232e24")
parse_lat("-45.23232e2")

# numeric input
parse_lat(1:10)
parse_lat(85:94)

# different formats
parse_lat("40.4183318 N")
parse_lat("40.4183318 S")
parse_lat("40 25 5.994") # => 40.41833

parse_lat("40.4183318N")
parse_lat("N40.4183318")
parse_lat("40.4183318S")
parse_lat("S40.4183318")

parse_lat("N 39 21.440") # => 39.35733
parse_lat("S 56 1.389") # => -56.02315

parse_lat("N40°25’5.994") # => 40.41833
parse_lat("40° 25´ 5.994\" N") # => 40.41833
parse_lat("40:25:6N")
parse_lat("40:25:5.994N")
parse_lat("40d 25’ 6\" N")
} # }
